key_insight: Specialist medical models still add value when combined with generalist LLMs and clinicians in a heterogeneous multi-agent system.
clinical_relevance: For clinical decision support, the study suggests better results may come from coordinating general reasoning, modality-specific analysis, and human oversight rather than relying on one all-purpose model.
method: Built HetMedAgent, a multi-agent framework pairing generalist LLMs with domain-specific specialist models.
Used conflict-aware evidence fusion to reconcile disagreements across agents.
Added uncertainty-based clinician intervention triggering and adaptive threshold calibration.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on three real-world clinical decision-making tasks and outperformed using either generalist or specialist models alone.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on reliable uncertainty calibration and safe clinician handoff rules, which may be difficult to implement consistently in practice.
paper_title: Why Specialist Models Still Matter: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Paradigm for Medical Artificial Intelligence
